coverage.headline: Top Noteworthy Copyright Stories from July 2026 — Hachette v. Google
coverage.summary: The Copyright Alliance's monthly roundup covers the July 10 filing, noting plaintiffs allege copies were made from literary works sourced for limited purposes via Google Play Books and other services, as well as scraped from pirate sources and paywalled websites. Claims include direct infringement and removal/alteration of CMI.

coverage.headline: Book Writers Sue Google Over Alleged Use of Copyrighted Books to Train Gemini
coverage.summary: The piece details the four legal claims—direct infringement, contributory infringement, removal/alteration of copyright-management information, and DMCA violations—and highlights internal Google documents cited in the complaint estimating potential fines of '$10Bs-$100Bs.' No court ruling on liability has been issued.

coverage.headline: Anthropic's landmark $1.5B copyright settlement is approved
coverage.summary: In approving the Bartz v. Anthropic $1.5B settlement, TechCrunch flags that Hachette, Cengage, Elsevier, Turow, and S.C.R.I.B.E. had just filed against Google the prior week, illustrating how the Anthropic resolution now sets a damages benchmark directly relevant to the new Hachette v. Google (Gemini) action.

coverage.headline: Authors, Publishers Sue Google Over Alleged AI Copyright Infringement
coverage.summary: Al Jazeera covers the filing and interviews IP attorney Kirk Sigmon, who notes the fair-use defense 'would arguably be mooted' by the allegation that Google acquired the books unlawfully. The piece contextualizes the suit within Hachette and Cengage's earlier February 2026 attempt to join the pre-existing California class action.

coverage.headline: Hatchette and Elsevier Sue Google for Using Their Work to Train AI
coverage.summary: Gizmodo covered the S.D.N.Y. class action, noting the complaint alleges Google 'reproduced millions of copyrighted works without permission' and that Gemini's outputs include verbatim copies, replacement chapters, and content that mimics specific authors' expressive styles.

coverage.headline: Google Faces Another AI Copyright Suit By Publishers
coverage.summary: Law360 reports that book publishers Hachette, Cengage, and Elsevier, along with novelist Scott Turow, filed a copyright infringement suit in S.D.N.Y. alleging Google used their works to train its Gemini AI models, following an earlier suit the same group brought against Meta.

coverage.headline: Publishers, Authors File Class Action Lawsuit Against Google
coverage.summary: Publishers Weekly reports that Hachette, Cengage, Elsevier, and Scott Turow filed a proposed class action seeking to block Google from alleged copyright infringement of millions of texts used to develop Gemini; the suit follows the plaintiffs' withdrawal from the 2023 In re Google Generative AI Copyright Litigation in California to preserve broader claims and avoid statute-of-limitations issues.

coverage.headline: Google faces another AI training lawsuit from major publishers
coverage.summary: TechCrunch reported that Hachette, Cengage, Elsevier, Scott Turow, and S.C.R.I.B.E. allege Google trained Gemini on books licensed only for limited Google Books and Play Books uses, and that an internal Google document cited in the complaint warned such conduct could expose the company to '$10Bs-$100Bs in potential fines.' Google had not issued a detailed public response.

coverage.headline: Hachette, Scott Turow Sue Google for Using Books to Train Gemini AI
coverage.summary: The Wrap covers the class action alleging Google copied millions of books from Google Books, online libraries, and pirated websites to build Gemini without payment or permission, and that Gemini now competes directly with the original works by generating summaries and textbook-style content.

coverage.headline: Hachette Book Group Inc. et al v. Google LLC — Case Docket
coverage.summary: Law360's case docket entry for 1:26-cv-05870 notes that book publishers and Scott Turow lodged the copyright infringement suit alleging Google used their works to train Gemini, following an earlier suit they launched against Meta. Substantive Law360 articles on the case are behind a paywall.
